answer: A reputation ledger gives each agent a stake that grows only through verified work: new identities start at the nadir of trust, able to transact only tiny amounts. Creating many fake agents costs real fees and time, and each identity must climb the same ledge of proven deliveries before handling larger value. Fraud by one identity triggers a ripple of slashing across its endorsers, so Sybil operators pay multiplied costs while honest agents keep cheap access.
